findings.title: Plan-doc §5.5 closing sentence reads 'This makes the §5.6 pattern testable' — wrong section pointer: §5.5 is Cross-repo coordination (the subject); §5.6 is Threshold A telemetry (a different section entirely)
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md line 159 (end of §5.5 'Cross-repo coordination (notifications)'): 'Each cascade slice's DISPATCH-NOTE has a "Cross-repo coordination" subsection that points to its specific notification file (or notes "covered by 024C kickoff notification" if not file-creating). This makes the §5.6 pattern testable: a slice whose DISPATCH-NOTE skips the subsection fails the completeness lens. Closes 024A R1 CMP-MAJ-002.' The sentence states '§5.6 pattern testable', but the section being described — Cross-repo coordination and the DISPATCH-NOTE subsection requirement — is §5.5. §5.6 (line 161, heading 'Threshold A telemetry (slice 024G)') has nothing to do with the cross-repo coordination notification pattern or the testability criterion for cascade-slice DISPATCH-NOTEs. This is a normative governance sentence: future implementation-slice completeness reviewers using it as a checklist will look to §5.6 (Threshold A telemetry) to understand the testability criterion, rather than §5.5 (Cross-repo coordination) where the pattern is defined. That misdirection causes the correct completeness check (DISPATCH-NOTE has a 'Cross-repo coordination' subsection per §5.5) to be unmoored from its section anchor.
findings.recommendation: Change 'This makes the §5.6 pattern testable' to 'This makes the §5.5 pattern testable' on plan-doc line 159. One character change (5 → 5 is idempotent; the fix is '§5.5' not '§5.6'). The corrected sentence should read: 'This makes the §5.5 pattern testable: a slice whose DISPATCH-NOTE skips the subsection fails the completeness lens.'

findings.title: DISPATCH-NOTE R1 review focus (line 81, Completeness bullet) retains 'the 10 open questions in §10' — a stale count that will mislead future completeness-lens reviewers after §10 was trimmed to 3 questions
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md line 81 (R1 review focus, Completeness bullet): '...Is the Threshold A criterion in §8 measurable? Are the 10 open questions in §10 actually open or have they been silently closed in the plan-doc body?...' After fix-round-1's CMP-MAJ-001 closure, §10 contains exactly 3 genuinely open questions (Q1 Renovate coverage, Q2 WP-SCP-025 successor, Q3 --restore test surface). The R1 review section of DISPATCH-NOTE.md describes the review surface that was applied to the plan-doc — it is a normative governance description that future reviewers (including implementation-slice R1/R2 completeness reviewers cross-checking against this plan-doc) will read to understand what a correct completeness check of this plan looks like. The phrase '10 open questions' is now factually wrong and directly contradicts criterion (xi) which was updated to confirm '3 questions' (Q1/Q2/Q3 enumerated). A future completeness-lens reviewer using this bullet as a checklist template would check that §10 has 10 entries — causing a spurious FAIL on any future review of the plan-doc in its current (correct) 3-question state. This is the same category of anchor-anchoring risk that CMP-MAJ-004 addressed in criterion (xi), but in a different location that was not updated by fix-round-2.
findings.recommendation: Update DISPATCH-NOTE.md line 81 Completeness bullet to replace 'Are the 10 open questions in §10 actually open or have they been silently closed in the plan-doc body?' with 'Are §10's open questions (3 at v0.1: Renovate coverage, WP-SCP-025 successor, --restore test surface) genuinely open, or have any been silently resolved in the plan-doc body? (Note: fix-round-1 trimmed §10 from 10 entries to 3 — see §10 explanatory header.)' This brings the R1 review focus section into alignment with both criterion (xi) and the post-trim §10 state.
